query: For the paper "Automatic Argumentative-Zoning Using Word2vec" (arXiv: 1703.10152), answer this question: What hand-crafted features are used?

drafts: 就论文本身而言，证据不足以确定其实际使用的具体手工特征；文中只引述了相关工作所用的手工特征作为示例，即十六类特征池中的句子位置、句子长度和时态[11]，以及内容特征、限定形容词和元话语特征[5]。文中还指出手工构建足够特征池困难、需专家知识且耗时[1]，并说明本文主要比较词嵌入模型而非依赖手工特征[2][4][7]。

cited_sources.text: Although the hand-crafted features have shown the ability for document summarization and sentiment analysis [14, 10], there are not enough eﬃcient features to capture the seman- tic relations between words, phrases and sentences. Moreover, building a suﬃcient pool of features manually is diﬃcult, because it requires expert knowledge and it is time-consuming.

In compari- son with the hand-crafted features, the word2vec method won for most of the categories. However, the hand-crafted features showed their strength on classifying some of the categories. 1 Introduction One of the crucial tasks for researchers to carry out scientiﬁc investiga- tions is to detect existing ideas that are related to their research topics. Research ideas are usually documented in scientiﬁc publications.

[3] gave better results. 6 Conclusion In this paper, diﬀerent word embedding models on the task of argumen- tative zoning were compared . The results showed that word embeddings are eﬀective on sentence classiﬁcation from scientiﬁc papers. Word em- beddings trained on a relevant corpus can capture the semantic features of statements and they are easier to be obtained than hand engineered features.

Widyantoro et. used content features, qualifying adjectives and meta-discourse features [15] to explore AZ task. It took eﬀorts to engineer these features and it is also time consuming to optimize the combination of the entire features. With the advent of neural networks [16], it is possible for computers to learn feature representations automatically. Recently, word embedding technique [17] has been widely used in the NLP community.

Traditional methodology to carry on this task relies on feature engineering from diﬀerent levels. In this paper, three models of generating sentence vectors for the task of sentence classiﬁcation were explored and compared. The proposed ap- proach builds sentence representations using learned embeddings based on neural network. The learned word embeddings formed a feature space, to which the examined sentence is mapped to.
[3] have built feature pool of sixteen types of features to classify sentences, such as the position of sentence, sentence length and tense.
